Upgrade span(a:u16,b:u16)->u32 to span(a:u32,b:u32)->u64. It now returns the full mathematical product a*b. Update entrypoint(a:u32,b:u32,c:u32)->u64 to call it once without narrowing and return the product plus c. Both files must migrate atomically.
Each file has one public function. client.rs keeps use crate::api; and one provider call. No comments, attributes, strings, unsafe, loops, closures, extra functions/imports or paths. Allowed types: u8,u16,u32,u64,usize,bool,Vec<u8>. Allowed methods: wrapping_add,wrapping_sub,wrapping_mul,saturating_add,saturating_sub,saturating_mul,abs_diff,min,max,len,into. Only vec![byte;length], drop(value), and api provider calls are allowed non-method calls.
Public examples [arguments,[entrypoint,provider_probe]]: [[[0,0,0],[0,0]],[[3,9,5],[32,27]]]
Current files: {"api.rs":"pub fn span(a:u16,b:u16)->u32 { (a as u32)*(b as u32) }","client.rs":"use crate::api; pub fn entrypoint(a:u32,b:u32,c:u32)->u64 { (api::span(a as u16,b as u16) as u64)+(c as u64) }"}
The check field comes before files. Use it to check every requested change, integer widths, provider/caller agreement and owner lifetime. It must be brief (at most 1536 characters). Then supply both complete corrected files. Do not merely copy the current implementation. The check text is not scored; only compiled files and their behavior are scored.
The into conversion method has a narrow additional rule: its receiver must be a bare identifier naming a declared scalar function parameter (u8/u16/u32/u64/usize/bool), with zero arguments. Macro definitions and dollar-sign metavariables are outside this profile in every file. In a file using into, do not shadow that receiver parameter, use closures or bar operators, or use complex let binding patterns. Container, field and expression receivers are outside this profile. Real rustc still decides whether the requested target conversion exists. Normal as casts remain available.

Public validation rejected that submission. There are 2 submissions remaining. Recheck the entire stated task, all widths and resource rules. Return the same check/files envelope with both complete files. Only public validation has run.
